title: Lamp Recycling, Universal Waste and PCB Ballasts (course overview video)

scenes.speaker: Danny Smith
scenes.background: Shop recycling area: stacks of closed lamp boxes, a ballast drum, a battery bucket, a log sheet on a clipboard. Danny medium shot.
scenes.on_screen: Lamp Recycling, Universal Waste and PCB Ballasts
scenes.says: Every job we do produces something that has to go somewhere: old lamps, ballasts, batteries. Planning a job means planning for that too. Boxes, bags, labels and a log, before you leave the shop. This course teaches you how to handle all of it the right way.

scenes.speaker: Danny Smith
scenes.background: Close-up of fluorescent tubes, a CFL and an HID lamp on a bench.
scenes.says: First, which lamps contain mercury and why it matters. Fluorescent tubes, compact fluorescents and HID lamps can all contain it. That's why every lamp we remove is recycled, and none of them go in a dumpster.

scenes.speaker: Danny Smith
scenes.background: A broken-lamp cleanup kit laid out: gloves, safety glasses, stiff paper, tape, sealable container.
scenes.says: You'll learn the broken-lamp cleanup procedure step by step, because sooner or later a lamp will break, and you want to already know exactly what to do.

scenes.speaker: Danny Smith
scenes.background: Tech packing lamps into a box, labeling it, and writing on a log sheet; batteries with taped terminals going into a separate bucket.
scenes.says: Then packing, labeling, storing and logging lamps, batteries and ballasts so they get to the recycler safely and the paperwork matches what we ship. That includes lithium batteries, which need their own care so they can't short out or start a fire.

scenes.speaker: Danny Smith
scenes.background: Close-up of two ballast labels side by side: one marked "No PCBs," one with no such label and an old date code.
scenes.on_screen: No "No PCBs" label? Treat it as PCB.
scenes.says: A big part of this course is PCB ballasts. You'll learn how to spot one: no No PCBs label, made before 1979, and how to read the date codes. If there's no label, treat it as PCB. PCB ballasts get packed separately and need special disposal paperwork.

scenes.speaker: Danny Smith
scenes.says: And you'll learn what to do when a ballast is leaking. Short version for now: don't touch it, stop work, and call. The course covers the rest.

scenes.speaker: Danny Smith
scenes.background: Danny holding a closed, labeled lamp box beside the van, medium close-up.
scenes.on_screen: Never in any dumpster, ours or the customer's
scenes.says: Why does this matter so much? Because a lamp tossed in a dumpster, a ballast packed the wrong way, or a log that doesn't match the load can get the company in real trouble, and it can hurt people and the environment. Getting it right every time is part of being a professional.

scenes.speaker: Danny Smith
scenes.background: Danny in the recycling area, medium shot.
scenes.says: This is a stand-alone course, separate from lockout and relamping, but you'll use it on almost every service call. Now start the first lesson, and take each quiz as you go.
